events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Agents

options.text: I will move my Scout adjacent to a rival Nation's territory, and establish an Agent Network!

events.text: With a Spymaster on your Council, you can convert [unit] into an Agent Network in a rival City (temporarily consuming the [unit] in the process). If you move your [unit] adjacent to the territory of that City, the Agent Network icon(CREATE_AGENT_NETWORK) button will be enabled in the Unit Panel on the left. An eligible Character can then be assigned as the local Agent for that City.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Anchoring

options.text: I will Anchored Ship Units to move my armies cross open water!

events.text: Ship Units, like the Bireme, Trireme, and Dromon, can Anchored to enable Land Units to move over water tiles. Without the help of an Anchored Ship, Land Units can only move through water Tiles within their nation's territory. Anchored comes at the cost of one Orders, and puts the Ship Unit on Cooldown. Land Units may move over water within the movement range of the Anchored Ship, starting on the turn after the Ship in question has Anchored. The Anchored status of a Ship persists until it is moved. Anchored a Ship by pressing the icon(ANCHOR) button in it's Action Panel on the left side of the screen while the Ship Unit is selected.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Axeman Selected

options.text: I can hit up to three enemies at once!

events.text: Your nation has trained its first Axeman. This Unit has an arcing Cleave attack, striking foes adjacent to its target for partial damage.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Chariot

options.text: Using Mounted Units to finish off enemies is the way to go!

events.text: Your nation has trained its first Mounted Melee Unit! These Units move quickly and have the unique ability to Rout your enemies, allowing you an additional attack if the first one destroys a Unit.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Onager Selected

options.text: I can hit up to seven enemies at once!

events.text: You have trained your first Onager. This Ranged Siege Unit has splash damage, so it will hurt all enemies adjacent to the target Tile.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Scout Selected

options.text: I'll use my Scout to explore the world!

events.text: Scout are fantastic explorers that can see further into the unknown than other Units. They can also hide in Trees, making them invaluable as an early warning against invading enemies. Send your Scout out into the wilderness to look for new City Site and mysterious Ancient Ruins. Scout (as well as Settler and Worker) can also Harvest Resource.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Spearman Selected

options.text: I'll use Spearmen to combat Mounted Units!

events.text: The Spearman is the first Polearm Unit available to your nation. Polearm Units excel against enemy Mounted Units. Only Polearm Units can exert a Zoc on Mounted Units. Spearman also have a Pierce attack, striking the unit behind their target for partial damage.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: The Caravan

options.text: I'll send my Caravan on a Caravan Mission!

events.text: Caravan Units can be sent on a Caravan Mission to a Foreign Capital. Upon safe arrival, the Caravan is consumed, and you receive a lump sum of Money. A successful Caravan Mission also results in an Opinion Player boost from their Nation. Be sure to protect your Caravan enroute to their destination as they are quite vulnerable to attack!

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: The Slinger
events.text: The Slinger is a Ranged Unit with a default maximum range of two Tiles. Ranged Units can shoot farther from on top of a Hill but suffer a int(DISTANCE_MODIFIER)% damage reduction for every Tile between them and their target. Firing into Trees or Scrub also reduces their damage.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: The Worker
events.text: Worker build Improvements for your City. Rural Improvements, such as Farm and Mine, gather raw materials. Urban Improvements, such as Barracks or Shrine, provide Training or Culture. With some exceptions, Urban Improvement must be built on or adjacent to other Urban Tiles. Improvement output can be augmented with Specialist from the City Screen.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Unit Upgrades

options.text: I'll Promotion and Upgrade my Units to prepare them for combat!

events.text: Units can receive both Upgrade and Promotion. Upgrade convert a Unit to a different type. For example, a Warrior can be Upgrade to an Spearman. Promotion provide various combat buffs. Both Promotion and Upgrade cost Training. Upgrade can only be performed inside of friendly territory while Promotion can be done anywhere.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Unit Upgrades

options.text: I'll Promotion and Upgrade my Units to prepare them for combat!

events.text: Units can receive both Upgrade and Promotion. Upgrade convert a Unit to a different type. For example, a Warrior can be Upgrade to an Axeman. Promotion provide various combat buffs. Both Promotion and Upgrade cost Training. Upgrade can only be performed inside of friendly territory while Promotion can be done anywhere.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Warrior Selected

options.text: I'll use Warriors for early combat!

events.text: The Warrior is the first Melee Unit available to your nation. Melee Units will form the backbone of your army, defending you from enemy Tribe and Nation.
